author: Looma Team
note: Starter posts written by the Looma team to begin conversations. They are NOT stories from real users and must be shown as official Looma Team posts.

posts.title: What is one small thing that helped you feel better this week?
posts.content: It does not have to be big. A walk after maghrib, a hot teh tarik, saying no to something, calling a friend. Share one thing that helped, even a tiny one. Someone reading might need that idea today.

posts.title: Cannot sleep again. What actually works for you?
posts.content: Some nights my mind will not stop. Phone away, warm shower, writing the worries on paper, a slow podcast: what has worked for you, and what did not? If it keeps going for weeks, it is also okay to talk to a doctor. You are not being dramatic.

posts.title: Period pain in class or at work: how do you cope?
posts.content: Many of us push through it quietly. What helps you? Heat pads, stretching, a certain tea, telling a lecturer or manager? Share your tips. Very strong pain is worth showing to a doctor, because you deserve proper care.

posts.title: Tired all the time? Be kind to yourself first
posts.content: Being tired for weeks is common when we are stressed, not eating or sleeping well, or doing too much for everyone. Small steps: regular meals, water, a short walk, one proper rest day. If it does not improve, a check-up can find simple causes. How do you look after your energy?

posts.title: Exam stress is eating me up. How do you study without burning out?
posts.content: I have a lot to revise and my head feels full. What do you do? Study plans, short breaks, study groups, putting the phone in another room? Also tell us how you calm down before an exam.

posts.title: Group assignment and I am doing all the work
posts.content: Has this happened to you? You message the group, a few people reply late, and you end up doing most of it. How did you handle it: split tasks in writing, tell the lecturer, or just finish it? What would you do differently?

posts.title: Thinking of changing course or continuing to a master's. How did you decide?
posts.content: Family has opinions, friends have opinions, and I am still not sure. If you made a big study decision, what helped you decide? What do you wish you had asked yourself earlier?

posts.title: Tips for speaking up in class when you are shy
posts.content: Starting small helps: prepare one question before class, sit near the front, ask after class if the room feels too big. What worked for you? Even sharing that you also feel nervous can help someone else.

posts.title: A colleague takes credit for my work. How do I speak up?
posts.content: A few ideas: send a short email after meetings listing what you did, share progress with your manager in writing, and say calmly, 'I worked on this part, happy to explain.' Have you tried these? What happened?

posts.title: First job interview next week. What do you wish you had known?
posts.content: Share your best tips: how to prepare, questions to ask the company, what to wear, how to handle the 'tell me about yourself' question. Nerves are normal. Everyone started somewhere.

posts.title: How do you ask for a raise without feeling awkward?
posts.content: Many of us are taught not to ask. Some ideas: note your results over the year, check what similar roles pay, pick a calm time, and ask for a short meeting. Have you done it? What did you say, and how did it go?

posts.title: Balancing family expectations and your career
posts.content: Sometimes the question is not 'can I do it' but 'will they accept it'. Working late, moving cities, staying single, or choosing a job family does not understand. How do you talk with your family about your goals?

posts.title: Getting home late: what are your safety habits?
posts.content: Share what you do. Examples: share your live location with a friend, wait for the ride inside a shop, check the driver's plate before getting in, keep your phone charged, walk in lit areas. Add your own so we can all learn.

posts.title: A stranger online is pressuring me for photos. What should I do?
posts.content: You do not owe anyone photos. Do not send anything. Save screenshots, block the person, and report the account on the app. If you feel threatened, tell someone you trust and look at the Get help tab for people you can call. It is never your fault.

posts.title: A note from the Looma Team: when to ask for help
posts.content: Talking here is good, but some situations need a real person: if you or someone is in danger, if you are being hurt or controlled, or if you feel you cannot go on. Please open the Get help tab and call. In an emergency call 999. You deserve support, and you do not have to be 'serious enough' to reach out.

replies.content: Looma Team: thank you for sharing. Small things count. We will read every reply.
Looma Team: keeping a private note of dates and tasks can really help if you ever need to explain your work.
Looma Team: a simple extra: tell one person your route and your ETA, and ask them to check on you.
